cards.text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster, so it's made to be sung. A whole group is praying over one person facing a day of trouble, and they start by asking the LORD to answer. It's like the group chat flooding you with prayer hands before your big day, except this group chat has a CHOIR.

cards.question: Then they call on the name of the God of Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). What do they ask that name to do for the person in trouble?

cards.text: Next they pray that God will send help from the sanctuary and hold this person up from Zion. Help straight from God's own house. No hold music. No 'please leave a message.'
Then they bring up this person's gifts and burnt offerings. This choir isn't skimming the file, friend. They're going through EVERY page.

cards.question: The group asks the LORD to remember this person's gifts. True or false: they also ask Him to look favorably on this person's burnt offerings.

cards.text: Then a Selah lands right there in the song, and after it the prayers get BIG. They ask God to give this person the desires of their heart.

cards.question: The group has asked God to give this person their heart's desires. What do they pray for this person's plans?
The group pictures the day this person wins. True or false: they pray they'll get to keep it quiet.

cards.text: They pray they'll get to shout for joy and raise a banner in the name of their God, like a whole stadium waving one giant flag. And they ask the LORD to grant every request this person makes.

cards.question: Up to now, the psalm has been one 'may' after another. Then one voice says, 'Now I know.' Now he's ___ that the LORD saves His anointed.

cards.text: He's sure the LORD saves His anointed and answers him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand. Friend, MY right hand is half a mustache, and HIS right hand SAVES.
Then comes the big comparison: some trust in chariots, and others in horses. Sharp edges don't last forever, friend. Mine went soft, and I landed in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The group praying in this psalm doesn't trust in chariots or horses: we trust in the ___ of the LORD our God.
The ones who trust in chariots and horses collapse and fall. True or false: the ones who trust in the name of the LORD fall right beside them.
The last line finally names the person this whole psalm has been praying for. Who is it?

cards.text: Then they ask the LORD to answer them on the day they call. The song opened asking Him to answer, and it closes asking Him to answer again.

findings.problem: In verses 1 to 5 the group speaks blessings to the person ('May the LORD answer you,' 'May He send you help,' 'May He give you...'). They are not speaking to the LORD. Several cards turn these into requests made to God. Card 1: 'they start by asking the LORD to answer.' Card 2: 'What do they ask that name to do.' Card 3: 'they pray that God will send help.' Card 5: 'The group asks the LORD to remember.' Card 6: 'They ask God to give this person.' Card 7: 'The group has asked God... What do they pray.' Card 8: 'they pray they'll get to keep it quiet.' Card 9: 'They pray they'll get to shout... And they ask the LORD to grant.' Only verse 9 ('O LORD, save the king. Answer us') is spoken to the LORD.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: Card 4 says the group brings up 'this person's gifts and burnt offerings.' Card 5 then asks whether they also ask Him to look favorably on the burnt offerings, so card 4 has already given the answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 3 has four sentences: 'Next they pray...' / 'Help straight from God's own house.' / 'No hold music.' / 'No 'please leave a message.''

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 6 sets this up with 'after it the prayers get BIG,' and card 7 repeats the setup. That rules out the wrong answers 'That God slows them down' and 'That they stay small' before the baker reasons at all. These answers are also not believable inside a run of blessings.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question quotes 'Now I know' and then asks the baker to fill in 'Now he's ___.' That line rules out both wrong answers, 'unsure' and 'doubtful.' The two wrong answers also mean nearly the same thing, so the right answer is given away inside the card.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the verse's core action. Verse 7 is about trusting in military strength. Papa Dorin's edges wearing out and his landing in the drawer is about wear and being replaced, not about something he trusted in. The 'sharp edges' image also doesn't fit chariots and horses.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 16 says 'The song opened asking Him to answer, and it closes asking Him to answer again.' This isn't accurate. The opening is a blessing spoken to the person ('May the LORD answer you'). The close is a request spoken to the LORD ('Answer us on the day we call').

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.
